reference.source: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation / Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics
clinicalPearls: A ciliopathy defined by a combination of rod-cone dystrophy (retinitis pigmentosa), postaxial polydactyly, truncal obesity, hypogonadism, renal anomalies and learning difficulty
Progressive retinal dystrophy typically presents with night blindness in childhood, advancing to severe visual loss by early adulthood
Renal involvement, ranging from structural malformation to progressive dysfunction, is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality and warrants monitoring
Postaxial polydactyly and other digit anomalies are an early, visible clue often noted at birth
Caused by biallelic variants in one of many BBS genes encoding components of the BBSome and cilia-related machinery, with autosomal recessive inheritance and locus heterogeneity
Obesity of early childhood onset, hyperphagia, type 2 diabetes and dyslipidaemia reflect hypothalamic and metabolic dysfunction
Learning difficulty is common but variable, and some individuals have normal cognition
reference.pathophysiology: Bardet-Biedl syndrome is a ciliopathy caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in one of numerous BBS genes, many of which encode subunits of the BBSome, a protein complex that regulates trafficking of cargo to and from the primary cilium. Because primary cilia are present on most cell types and are essential for sensory function and developmental signalling, their dysfunction produces a pleiotropic, multisystem disorder affecting the retina, kidneys, limbs, reproductive system and hypothalamic appetite regulation. Locus and allelic heterogeneity, and occasional oligogenic contributions, account for the variable phenotype.
additionalDifferentials: Isolated retinitis pigmentosa or Leber congenital amaurosis
additionalInvestigations: Gene-panel or exome sequencing covering the BBS genes
Electroretinography and formal ophthalmological assessment to characterise the retinal dystrophy
Renal ultrasound and renal function testing with ongoing monitoring
Fasting glucose, HbA1c and lipid profile for metabolic complications
Blood pressure monitoring given renal and metabolic risk
Endocrine assessment of gonadal function and, in selected cases, hypothalamic function
redFlags: Declining renal function or hypertension signalling progressive nephropathy
Rapid visual deterioration requiring low-vision support
Features of poorly controlled diabetes or severe dyslipidaemia
reference.prognosis: Vision is usually severely impaired by adulthood, and long-term outlook is dominated by renal disease and the metabolic consequences of obesity and diabetes. With proactive renal and metabolic management, many individuals have a reasonable lifespan, though end-stage renal disease is an important cause of premature death.
pitfalls: Diagnosing isolated retinitis pigmentosa and missing the systemic ciliopathy
Overlooking silent progressive renal impairment until it is advanced
Attributing obesity to lifestyle alone rather than hypothalamic dysfunction
Confusing it with Alstrom syndrome, which lacks polydactyly but includes sensorineural deafness and cardiomyopathy
